learning_objective: 🎯 Trace the flow of solar energy and the cycling of critical nutrients through nature's complex, interconnected webs of life!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An ecosystem consists of biotic (living) and abiotic components working together. It has four basic functions: Productivity (making food), Decomposition (breaking down dead stuff), Energy Flow, and Nutrient Cycling.

Primary production is the amount of biomass created by plants (Producers). When things die, decomposers (fungi, bacteria, earthworms) break the complex organic matter down into simple inorganic nutrients (fragmentation, leaching, catabolism).
Sunlight is the ultimate energy source. Energy flows strictly in ONE direction (unidirectional) from plants to herbivores to carnivores. Interconnected food chains make up a highly stable Food Web.

Graphical representations of trophic levels. Pyramids of Number and Biomass can sometimes be inverted (like a single large tree supporting thousands of insects). BUT the Pyramid of Energy is ALWAYS upright!

The gradual, predictable change in species composition in a given area over time. Primary succession starts on bare rock (very slow), while Secondary succession starts where a previous ecosystem was destroyed by fire or flood (much faster).

fun_activity.title: 💸 The 10% Tax Law
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine energy as money. Plants trap $100$ worth of solar energy. When a deer eats the plant, it only gets $10$. When a tiger eats the deer, it only gets $1$. The '10% Law' explains why food chains rarely go beyond 4 or 5 levels—there just isn't enough energy left!

exam_tips: 📌 The steps of decomposition are a guaranteed topic: Fragmentation -> Leaching -> Catabolism -> Humification -> Mineralization.
📌 ALWAYS emphasize that the pyramid of energy is upright because energy is lost as heat at every single step, following the second law of thermodynamics.
📌 Differentiate between Hydrarch succession (starts in water, moves to land) and Xerarch succession (starts on dry rock, moves to forest). Both culminate in a stable 'mesic' forest community.
quick_recap: ⭐ Earthworms are called the 'farmer's friends' because they break down detritus into smaller particles (fragmentation) and loosen the soil.
⭐ The detritus food chain (starting with dead organic matter) is actually much more significant in terrestrial ecosystems than the grazing food chain.
⭐ Phosphorus is a sedimentary cycle (stored in rocks), while Carbon is a gaseous cycle (stored in the atmosphere and oceans).
